newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Kia Group automakers to stop plants for two days.
newsitem.headline: Kia Group automakers to stop plants for two days.

text.p: Kia Motors Corp and Asia Motors Corp, both units of South Korea's troubled Kia Group, plan to suspend production on Monday and Tuesday for maintenance, a Kia Group spokesman said on Saturday.
"We decided to undertake maintenance on all production lines of the two companies on August 4 and 5 as we had done at around this time in the past," said Jeun Sang-jin.
Operations at the plants would stop for four straight days because workers were taking weekend holidays from Saturday, he said.
He denied local news reports that the plan was linked to reported problems facing subcontractors of the two automakers in the aftermath of the group's financial troubles.
The troubles of the Kia Group, the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate, have been mainly due to slumping domestic vehicle sales at a time when debts were mounting.
On July 15, Kia's creditor banks selected the group for protection from an immediate bankruptcy because they thought the group would be unable to avoid defaults on debt payments.
Friday's meeting of creditors failed to produce results after creditors determined that the group's self-rescue plans were not satisfactory.
The group has refused demands by creditors to promise the unconditional resignation of the group's top executives.
Creditors are due to meet again on Monday to detail their July 15 decision to offer protection.
